problem: A 200-character body paragraph is set in Bodoni Moda at 28 px across a 76ch measure. `.nv-prose--wide` is 76ch and `.nv-h3` is `--type-h3` (Bodoni 400 / 28 px), so the line box runs roughly 1,060 px inside a 1,296 px container — about 90–100 characters per line in a high-contrast didone. The design system reserves Bodoni for display and caps prose at 64ch (`--container-text`); this is Bodoni doing body-copy duty at an unreadable measure.

fix:
Either set it as body — `

` (Archivo Light, `--fs-body-lg`, 64ch) — or, if the intent is a statement, keep `.nv-h3` and cap it at `max-width: 34ch` and trim to the first clause, moving the country list into the `.nv-tag` row that already sits below it. Do not leave a 76ch Bodoni paragraph.

problem: Portrait 4:5 frames are fed landscape source photographs that are physically smaller than the frame, so the mill photography is upscaled and severely cropped. `quienessomos_foto_1/2/3` are 416×372 px rendered into a 416×520 frame (each grid-3 column is exactly 416 px at the 1440 container), forcing a 1.40× scale and a 40 % horizontal crop. Worse, the Filosofía aside puts `quienessomos_foto_4` (416×300) into a ~524 px-wide 4:5 frame — a 2.18× upscale before the display's device pixel ratio is even applied. The design direction calls for visible texture and grain; at that magnification the weave detail is gone.
evidence: nosotros.html:118, 130, 142 `<figure class="nv-figure nv-figure--4x5 …">` around `quienessomos_foto_1.jpg` (416×372), `_2` (416×372), `_3` (416×372); nosotros.html:246 the same class around `quienessomos_foto_4.jpg` (416×300); nosotros.html:518, 530, 542 around `quienessomos_foto_7/8/9.jpg` (416×300). site.css:848 `.nv-figure--4x5 { --fig-ratio: 4 / 5; }` with site.css:861–864 `object-fit: cover`.
fix: Match the frame to the asset: use `nv-figure--3x2` (1.50, closest to the 416×300 native 1.387) for the `_4/_7/_8/_9` figures and `nv-figure--4x3`-equivalent (add `--fig-ratio: 4 / 3` alongside the existing modifiers) for the 416×372 people shots. Reserve `--4x5` for sources that are actually portrait. Same six figures in en/about.html.

problem: The fifth key-figure tile overflows its column. At the 1440 container the strip is five equal 259.2 px columns; tiles 2–5 carry 24 px inline padding, leaving 211.2 px of content width. `1,000,000+ sq ft` at `clamp(24px, 2.6vw, 40px)` monospace (37.4 px at 1440, ~0.6 em advance) needs ~360 px and the first unbreakable run `1,000,000+` alone needs ~225 px — it overflows the tile and then breaks across three lines. The ES page is not overflowing but orphans the unit: `100,000+ m²` drops `m²` onto its own line, so the number and its unit are visually divorced, which the system explicitly forbids.
evidence: en/index.html:158–161 `<dd class="nv-figures__num">1,000,000+ sq ft</dd>`; index.html:160 `<dd class="nv-figures__num">100,000+ m²</dd>`; site.css:904–911 `.nv-figures__num { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: clamp(24px, 2.6vw, var(--fs-display-3)); }` inside site.css:884 `grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr))`.
fix:
Split the unit out and shrink the cap: mark up as `
1,000,000+sq ft
` and add `.nv-figures__num { font-size: clamp(20px, 2vw, var(--fs-display-4)); white-space: nowrap; } .nv-figures__unit { display: block; font-size: var(--fs-body-sm); }`. Apply to both language homes so `100,000+ m²` and `1,000,000+ sq ft` set identically.

problem: Headline casing is inconsistent within single pages and contradicts the design system's "sentence case for headlines, never Title Case A Whole Headline" rule. The clearest self-contradiction: the nav and footer link says "Quiénes somos" while the page's own h1 says "Quiénes Somos". Across the ES tree, Title-Cased headlines sit next to sentence-cased ones in the same scroll.

Quiénes Somos

` vs index.html:47 `Quiénes somos`. Other Title-Cased headings: nosotros.html:394 `Compromiso y Política Ambiental`, nosotros.html:481 `Política de Calidad`, index.html:170 `Nuestra Historia`, index.html:315 `Video Corporativo`, productos.html:97 `Nuestros Productos`, procesos.html:99 `Nuestros Procesos`, procesos.html:222 `Teñido y Acabado` — all beside sentence-cased siblings such as `Integración vertical`, `Nuestra gente`, `Familias de tela`, `Nuestro grupo`, `Todo el proceso productivo`.

Proper nouns (San Ildefonso, Novalan, Don Juan Morera, Familia Morera) keep their capitals. problem: The hero plinth — the paper shelf under the hero image that every other page uses to hold a left-hand fact and a right-hand scroll cue — is inconsistent across the five pages. nosotros/en-about ship only the cue, and because `.nv-hero__plinth` is `display:flex; justify-content:space-between`, a lone child lands at the *left* edge, so the cue jumps sides relative to index/productos/procesos. contacto/en-contact drop the plinth entirely, so the contact hero has no shelf and no cue at all. Combined with three different hero ratios (`nv-hero` 21:9, `nv-hero--compact` 21:7, `nv-hero--16x9` 16:9), the hero reads as a different component on each page.

` containing only ``; contacto.html:85–101 — `

8 valores

problem: The page closes with three navigations stacked inside the last screen and a half: the "Secciones" card row, the ink CTA band, and the footer's Navegación column — plus the sticky header nav still on screen. problem: The address, both phone numbers and the e-mail are printed twice in the last 700 px of every non-contact page: once in the ink CTA band and again in the ink footer's Contacto column, in the same ink treatment. Because `.nv-footer` carries `margin-block-start: var(--section-y)`, a 96 px stripe of paper separates the two ink blocks, so the repetition reads as an accident rather than a deliberate coda.

The footer's Navegación and Grupo columns are unaffected.

problem: Thirteen fabric families in a fixed 3-up grid produce four full rows and one orphan card sitting alone at the left of row five, with two empty columns beside it. On a page whose entire argument is the completeness of the range, the grid ends on a visual stumble.

problem: The right-hand card is a decorative panel standing in for a map: a herringbone weave texture with two crossed hairlines and a pin square at the centre, carrying no geographic information at all. The crosshair centres on nothing — the pin is at 50%/50% of an abstract field — so it reads as an unfinished placeholder rather than a designed plate, and it is the largest single element on the page.

That gives the card real content, uses an asset already on disk, and preserves the zero-network requirement that motivated the drawn plate.

problem: The yarns family is the only one of the thirteen whose `-1600` asset is not actually 1600 px: `assets/img/fabric/yarns-1600.jpg` is 800×452. The lightbox opens it as the full-screen view and the dialog markup declares `width="1600" height="842"`, so the image is upscaled roughly 2× on a desktop viewport and is visibly softer than the other twelve slides, and the declared intrinsic ratio (1.90) does not match the file (1.77), producing a reflow the moment the real image decodes.
evidence: productos.html:456 `data-nv-src="assets/img/fabric/yarns-1600.jpg"` (file measures 800×452, while every other `-1600` measures 1600×842); productos.html:642 ``. Same at en/products.html.
fix: Two parts. (1) Ask for a true 1600×842 `yarns-1600` crop, or point the yarns opener at `yarns-800.jpg` so the lightbox is not asked to upscale. (2) Stop hard-coding the dialog's dimensions to one family's ratio — have site.js set `width`/`height` from `data-nv-w` / `data-nv-h` attributes carried by each opener, alongside the `data-nv-src` it already reads in `render()` (assets/js/site.js:180–195).

problem: The lightbox image ships with an empty `src` attribute. An empty `src` is not a no-op: several browsers resolve it against the document URL and issue a second request for the HTML page itself, which is then decoded as an image and fails. It is invisible in normal use but it is a spurious network request on a site whose whole premise is zero network dependencies until the visitor clicks play.
evidence: productos.html:642 `` and productos.html:641 ``; same lines in en/products.html.
fix: Remove the empty `src` and `srcset` attributes entirely — site.js already sets both in `render()` before the dialog is shown (assets/js/site.js:188–192 `source.setAttribute('srcset', webp)` / `img.setAttribute('src', jpg)`), so nothing else has to change.

problem: The key-figures strip is five equal columns above 1180 px, and the English value `1,000,000+ sq ft` is set in `--font-mono` at `clamp(24px, 2.6vw, 40px)`. Digit groups separated by commas carry no line-break opportunity, so `1,000,000+` must fit on one line. Between roughly 1181 px and 1400 px the cell's content box (column width minus the 24 px inline padding) is narrower than that string — e.g. at a 1280 px viewport the cell content box is ~179 px while `1,000,000+` at 33 px monospace needs ~183–200 px depending on the fallback face — and the number spills across the hairline into the neighbouring cell. The Spanish counterpart (`100,000+ m²`, two characters shorter) fits.
evidence: en/index.html line 160 `<dd class="nv-figures__num">1,000,000+ sq ft</dd>` with site.css lines 878–905 `.nv-figures { grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); }` and `.nv-figures__num { font-size: clamp(24px, 2.6vw, var(--fs-display-3)); }`.
fix:
Lower the upper bound of the clamp for this strip, e.g. `.nv-figures__num { font-size: clamp(20px, 2.1vw, var(--fs-display-4)); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }`, or move the unit onto its own line by marking it up as `
1,000,000+sq ft
` with the unit set to `display: block`.
